claims.text: In situ pulsed-laser remelting during LPBF will relieve residual thermal stresses in AlCrFeNiSi components relative to continuous high-energy LPBF.
In situ pulsed-laser remelting will improve the mechanical properties of LPBF AlCrFeNiSi components.
The feedstock is pre-alloyed AlCrFeNiSi powder with morphology and composition suitable for LPBF.
The pulsed-laser remelting step is applied immediately after each deposited LPBF layer.
The proposed intervention is applicable to miniature components below approximately 5 mm in scale.
A low-energy pulsed-laser scheme with microsecond- to nanosecond-scale pulses and interlayer cooling can operate within the conventional LPBF processing window.
Pulsed-laser remelting will refine the AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
Pulsed-laser remelting will reduce grain size.
Pulsed-laser remelting will lower dislocation density.
Reduced grain size and lower dislocation density will minimize residual thermal gradients.
The pulsed laser locally remelts deposited AlCrFeNiSi material.
The locally remelted material rapidly resolidifies.
Local remelting and rapid resolidification relieve built-up thermal stresses.
Local remelting and rapid resolidification homogenize the microstructure.
Pulsed-laser-remelted samples will have higher yield strength than samples produced by continuous high-energy LPBF.
Pulsed-laser-remelted samples will have greater ductility than samples produced by continuous high-energy LPBF.
Integrating pulsed-laser remelting will reduce reliance on post-fabrication heat treatments and associated processing complexity.
The expected improvements may not transfer to larger components or non-optimized energy inputs.
